newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Cultus surges on hopes of new production.
newsitem.headline: Cultus surges on hopes of new production.

text.p: Shares in Cultus Petroleum NL shot to a fresh all-time high on Monday after reports of new "wildcat" oil wells fuelled speculation about the company's potential oil production.
Cultus spiked 33 cents higher to peak at NZ$3.55 before settling at NZ$3.48 by the close, a rise of 26 cents on the day.
"It's speculation about this drilling programme they have in New Zealand," said Tim Koller, broker at Merrill Lynch.

Last Thursday, Cultus managing director Don Beard told Reuters the company believed its Maari oilfield, offshore Taranaki on the west coast of New Zealand's North Island, could produce as much as 100 million barrels of black gold, which would make it one the country's largest oilfields.
"We see the potential for around about 100 million barrels of oil," Beard said.
He said the company hoped to start drilling at Maari in November or December this year, depending on the availability of rigs.
